QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_49

question.text: The Investment Manager of a Category III AIF may have incentive to take riskier or more speculative positions because:

answer.text: Higher incentive fees are earned on higher returns, tempting speculative bets
Hurdle rate falls automatically with risk
GST is exempt on speculative trades

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that the Investment Manager may choose riskier or more speculative investments compared with a Category III AIF's stated objectives in order to earn higher incentive fees. This is the classic principal-agent conflict tied to performance-linked compensation. The Trap: Option A is false because management fees are not driven by portfolio volatility. Options C and D are invented; hurdle rates do not fall automatically with risk, and there is no GST exemption for speculative trades. Note: Source page 175 supports the incentive-fee conflict; pages 149-150 cover the fee and expense structure.
